item.title: Self-Hosted Hydrologic Data Platforms: Tethys Platform vs HydroShare vs CUAHSI HydroClient
item.description:
Why Self-Host Hydrologic Data Management?

Water resource management depends on integrating diverse datasets — stream gauge readings, groundwater well logs, satellite precipitation estimates, climate model outputs, and water quality samples — into coherent analysis workflows. Historically, hydrologists spent more time locating and formatting data than actually analyzing it. Purpose-built hydrologic data platforms address this fragmentation by providing centralized catalogs, standardized metadata, and web-based visualization tools.

item.title: Self-Hosted Climate & Environmental Data Servers: THREDDS vs ESGF vs ERDDAP
item.description:
Introduction

Climate science and environmental monitoring generate petabytes of data annually — from satellite observations and weather models to ocean buoy readings and ice core samples. Making this data accessible to researchers worldwide requires specialized data servers that understand scientific data formats like NetCDF, HDF5, and GRIB, provide efficient subsetting and aggregation, and expose standardized web service interfaces.
